title: Post-loop hiring notes — Priya Nair
content:
Quick personal debrief after the interview loop for Priya Nair (applied: Senior Inference Engineer). Goal: capture first-pass thoughts, calibration notes for hiring committee, follow-ups I want to triage before formalizing the scorecard.

High-level gut: strong systems intuition, thoughtful tradeoffs on latency vs mem/cost. Not as battle-tested on distributed KV cache eviction strategies (we asked but didn't get deep design here). Communication: crisp, good analogies, slightly verbose in whiteboard sessions but organized.

Panel-by-panel notes (raw, unedited):
- Phone screen (Sam): solid background on model-serving pipelines; emphasized feature flags and rollouts; gave an example of a canary failure and how they diagnosed tail latency — good incident framing.
- Systems design (Priya + me): designed a micro-batching layer that balances request shaping and per-tenant fairness. Lacked concrete math for head-room calculation (I prompted for throughput calc but answer was heuristic).
- Inference runtime deep-dive (Aisha): strong on operator-level optimization (fused kernels, vectorization), weaker on cross-GPU KV-cache coherence (no prior at-scale coherence design).
- Culture / leadership (Liam): good mentorship anecdotes, described two reports and a gradual ownership handoff plan. Gave reasonable post-mortem structure.

Scorecard draft (0–4 scale, with short rationale) — this is my personal baseline:
- Technical breadth (system design, infra): 3 — good exposure across layers, some gaps in distributed cache protocols.
- Runtime internals / kernels: 3 — understands optimizations; limited production ownership of low-level kernel tuning at fleet scale.
- Reliability / SRE mindset: 3 — incident handling and runbooks present but lacking examples of proactive monitoring/prioritization tradeoffs.
- Product sense / customer impact: 4 — strong; connected infra choices to customer SLAs and cost.
- Communication & collaboration: 4 — very clear, actionable.
- Overall recommendation (lean): hire-limit (strong hire for mid-Senior, consider Senior+ with support on distributed-cache)

Risks and unknowns to surface in committee:
- No prior work designing coherent KV-cache across heterogeneous GPUs (we rely on this heavily for low-latency caching strategies).
- Quantization/precision tradeoffs: experience mostly with int8 offline; limited work on dynamic quantization in live serving.
- Scale of previous infra: most experience at 50–200 GPU clusters, not yet at 1000+ node fleets. Are they comfortable with the operational cadence we need?

Suggested follow-ups / homework before finalizing scorecard:
- Ask for a short write-up (1–2 pages) where Priya sketches a coherent KV-cache sync strategy for a multi-GPU model shard scenario (focus on correctness, tail-latency, and memory overhead). Deadline: 3 business days.
- Quick technical take-home: a small micro-benchmark script or pseudo-code showing how they'd measure and bound prefix-cache hit rate impact on token latency under varying QPS. (Optional but would help surface math).

Interview loop calibration notes (for internal use):
- Aisha tends to be conservative on kernel-level claims; weigh her comments accordingly.
- Liam prioritizes leadership examples; may overemphasize mentorship vs raw technical scope.
- Sam focuses on incident narratives; his positive note likely indicates Priya has good on-call instincts.

Logistics / EDGES:
- Compensation band: expect to be within Senior band; Priya asked about possibility of Senior+ given distributed infra experience is partial. Recommend aligning to Senior and revisiting after a 3–6 month expectations plan.
- Start date: flexible, 4–6 weeks notice.

Notes to self / interviewer's checklist for final committee doc:
- Consolidate panel excerpts into single paragraph per panel (2–3 sentences each).
- Add explicit examples for "scale gap" with questions we can ask at offer stage to set expectations (on-call hours, escalation path, break-glass scenarios).
- Capture Priya's GitHub repo pointers (she listed 2 repos; request links if not already in application).

Open questions I want resolved before thumbs-up:
1) Has she ever implemented a cross-node eviction policy where KV entries are serialized across shards and consistency is a requirement?
2) Examples of tuning for 99.9th percentile latency specifically attributable to memory GC or inter-GPU sync.
3) Any hands-on work with HSM/KMS integrations for private deployments (asked briefly, unclear).

Tone: treat this as a calibration note — not final. I'll draft the formal scorecard after we get the two short deliverables (write-up + repo links). If deliverables are solid, escalate to hire with Senior+ compensation carve-out.

Links / references I mentioned during interviews:
- internal doc: PROD-1234 (cache-coherency brief)
- example ticket we referenced: JIRA-4578 (canary rollback case)

Action items (me):
- Email Priya the write-up prompt and deadline (by EOD).
- Add panel excerpts to the scorecard template (by tomorrow).
- Ping Aisha for a 10-min follow-up to clarify kernel-level examples if deliverables are borderline.

End of notes.

Notes-to-self meta: keep language explicit in committee write-up about "known unknowns" — that will help set appropriate onboarding expectations and preempt escalation around 3-month entitlements.
